thread:
maria_cs: FYI - onboarding run for Vaultup is flapping: some requests to /v1/generate return 200, others 403. Customer is on our Node SDK v0.9.2 behind a corporate proxy.

maria_cs: Example from the customer (redacted token):
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXXXXX\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-small","input":"hello"}'
```

maria_cs: Response snippet when it fails:
```json
HTTP/2 403
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_auth\",
  \"message\": \"token missing or invalid for this route\"
}
```

dan_engineer: thanks — do we have any server-side logs for the failed request ids? can you grab the request-id header from the failing responses?

maria_cs: gave them the failing request-ids: req_17a2 and req_17a3. both returned same 403. they also said it only happens when they run on their desktop app (electron), not on prod servers.

isaac_net: quick suspicion: corporate proxy / http2 layer might be normalizing or dropping the Authorization header. some proxies rewrite headers for pseudoheaders or strip uppercase names when translating gRPC/http2<->http1. try forcing HTTP/1.1 from the client as a quick test.

dan_engineer: +1. ask them to run: `curl --http1.1 -v ...` and paste the raw response. if that fixes it it's almost certainly header mangling. also ask if the SDK is using the `http2-wrapper` or a custom fetch that may convert headers into pseudoheaders incorrectly.

maria_cs: customer ran the http1.1 curl and same token + payload -> 200, payload returned correctly. they said in electron it uses node's `http2` module via a third-party lib.

isaac_net: that nails it. some proxies (esp older enterprise appliances) will terminate HTTP/2 and re-emit to backend but accidentally drop `Authorization` when it's sent as a regular header on certain frames. two short workarounds:
- Force HTTP/1.1 from client (we can document this for onboarding).
- Configure their proxy to preserve `authorization` header (they'll need infra team to allow pass-through).

dan_engineer: for a patch on our side, we can add an SDK option `forceHttp1: true` (small change) and a runtime check that sends an extra `X-Auth-Hint: 1` header so proxies that are configured to whitelist that header will forward it. not ideal, but pragmatic for onboarding customers behind locked-down proxies. filing a tiny ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/patches/force-http1-sdks #1123 -> staging at 2025-11-10T16:30:00Z

maria_cs: customer accepted temp workaround (pin http1.1) and they were able to finish test suite. asked for a short note in onboarding docs and a line in the troubleshooting playbook.

isaac_net: two follow-ups for CS: 1) recommend they switch SDK usage in electron to the node `https` client (or enable HTTP/1.1 fallback), 2) tell infra to allow `authorization` passthrough. I'll add a KB entry describing the proxy symptom + curl reproducible test.

maria_cs: noted. also flagged account risk: was a bit worried because onboarding stalled for ~3 days, but they're green now. I'll mark renewal-risk as low and schedule a 1:1 enablement run with them next week.

dan_engineer: one more note — concurrency patterns can hide this (http2 multiplex will show intermittent failures). if they re-enable http2 later encourage limited concurrency ramp while testing to avoid hitting our rate windows unexpectedly (they saw a couple of 429 spikes when they retried aggressively).

maria_cs: copied. thanks everyone — I'll add the transcript and the curl reproducible steps to the customer's support ticket and close after doc updates. :thumbsup:

isaac_net: good catch. filing infra KB + small SDK flag.

maria_cs: closing loop with the customer now. thanks!
